with.line: Hungry? Eating is what mends you here.

script.text: You're awake. Good. Eat this first, talk after.

then.text: Rune Isle. Your ship hit the rocks under the lighthouse. They all do.
Follow the path up from the beach. There's a camp. Nothing on the path will hurt you.
I gave you a meal already. I sell them now: three gold.

else.text: Food is what mends you here. Hungry, you stay hurt. Fed, you heal.

traded.text: Eat it now. You'll feel it mend you.

then.text: Three gold a piece. Cooked this morning.
One gold a cut. I'll cook it.
Two gold a skin. Idris at the camp pays the same.
You won't die here. Nobody does. You'll wake up, and it will hurt, and you'll have lost something.
Usually something small. Wolves I can live with. If anyone tells you a troll is not so bad, they have not met one.
Tove. I hunt. I was born here, back when the island had a harbour and people still got old.
The light out there brought your ship in. Halvard built it to bring ships home. It still does, in its way.
Eat before you're hungry, not after.

with.line: Five skins for a cap! Boots before anything else!

script.text: Skins, {partner}? Leather for leather. That's how I sell.

then.text: Caps and helms. Every one of them starts as a skin — the iron is riveted onto my leather.
{item:leather-cap}. One point.

traded.text: Better than your hair. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:iron-helm}. Two points, and two more against blunt.

traded.text: That is what a helm is for. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:knights-helm}. Three points, and three more against sharp blows.

traded.text: You'll see less and live longer. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:wolfskin-hood}. One point, and three against sharp blows.

traded.text: Wear it with the ears up. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: As you like. What else?
Only one coat on my rack. The armourer has the rest.
{item:wolfskin-coat}. Two points, and five against sharp blows.

traded.text: A wolf could not bite through it. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: As you like. What else?
Boots. A good sole is a good hide, and I have the hides.
{item:worn-boots}. One point, and soft enough to walk in on the first day.

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:hobnailed-boots}. One point, and three against blunt.

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:steel-sabatons}. Two points, and two against sharp blows.

traded.text: Heavy, and worth it. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: {item:wolfskin-boots}. One point, and three against sharp blows.

traded.text: Quiet on the floor. What else?

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: Fair enough. What else?
{item:leather-backpack}. Eight more things carried, on your back where your hands stay free.

cancel.text: It stays on the hook, then. Anything else?

then.text: I'll pay gold for anything you cut off a beast. What have you got?
I'll pay you 2 gold per {item:skin} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:wolf-skin} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:bone} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:rat-tail} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:bat-wing} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:rabbit-foot} you have.
I'll pay you 2 gold per {item:snake-fang} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:imp-horn} you have.
I'll pay you 5 gold per {item:bear-claw} you have.
I'll pay you 6 gold per {item:troll-tusk} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:yeti-fur} you have.
I'll pay you 25 gold per {item:cyclops-eye} you have.
As you like. What else?
Idris. I came here as a saddler and stayed. There were no horses after the harbour went, so I make boots and jerkins.
Six deaths in a hundred and thirty years. That's a good record here. Ask Tove hers.
Wolves go for the legs first. Boots before anything else.

with.line: Stew's hot! Sit, eat!

script.text: Sit. Eat. You look like the sea chewed you.

then.text: Two gold a loaf.
Three gold. Off the fire just now.
Two gold a piece.
Bring me meat and I will pay you. One gold a cut.
Ifeoma. I ran the busiest eating house on the harbour, before the flood took it.
My sister is across the water. She will be old by now, or gone. I am fifty-two, and I will stay fifty-two.
That is Biscuit. Rats killed me once. Rats! Biscuit was not with me then.
Come back hungry.

onEnter.text: Where did I leave that trap...

script.text: Mind your feet. Some of what's in this grass is mine.

then.text: Traps. Nets on land, I call them. Rope and nails, and the wrecks bring both.
I've no trap ready to sell today. Ask me again another time.
Eleven times. Nine of them my own traps. I keep making them better, so it keeps hurting more.
Peregrine. Fisherman, born here. I had a wife. She died the winter before Halvard's rune, the old way, in her bed.
I think she was lucky. Her name went about my fifth death. Margit at the inn remembers my crew for me.
Watch the grass.

with.line: Fresh off the wreck! Lanterns and sacking!

script.text: Whatever was in your hold is mine now, unless you want to buy it back.

then.text: What came up off the wrecks. Lanterns and sacking.
A {item:sack}. Smells of the sea.
A {item:hand-lantern}. It still lights.
Right. What else?
Wenna. I was a shipwright's apprentice, born here. Nobody needs a ship that can't leave, so I take them apart.
Drowning's the bad one. Second worst on the island, they tell me. Three times now, working the wrecks.
Bring me anything that floats.

onEnter.text: Tails, wings, bones! I'll buy them!

script.text: Rat tails, bat wings, bones. I pay a little. The towns pay more, but the towns are a long way off.

then.text: Show me what you've got.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:rat-tail} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:bat-wing} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:rabbit-foot} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:bone} you have.
I'll pay you 2 gold per {item:snake-fang} you have.
Right. What else?
Jory. Harbour pickpocket, born and bred. Nobody can hang you here. I like that.
Brannoc killed me four times for one stolen knife. Fair, I suppose.
Human skull? Put that away. Somebody here knew them.
Mind your pockets.

script.text: Welcome to the temple town, {partner}. Carve what you like. Don't carve it at anyone.

then.text: Wolves come to the garden plots at night. Four gold for every {item:wolf-skin} you bring me.

traded.text: The plots thank you. Anything else?

then.text: I do. I was the harbour's magistrate. When it flooded I led these people up from the water.
I'm still leading them, a hundred and thirty years later. Nobody else has had the chance to try.
Break Wyrd, and Morwen is seventy and Peregrine is sixty, and both of them are a hundred and thirty years late.
Somebody should think about that before they climb.
Absalom was my captain of the watch. He took the people who refused runes east, and I let them go rather than fight.
Twelve deaths. Three of them were our own people, in the year before the split. Those are the ones I remember.
Go carefully, {partner}.

with.line: Bring me a blank and an essence.

script.text: Welcome to the temple, {partner}. Mind the forges; they are older than the town.

then.text: Bone takes the first forge, crystal the second, deep ore the third.
Shape your material into a blank there, then bring the blank to me.

options.label: What do you do with a blank?

then.text: I carve the mark. Bring an essence with it and the rune takes that element. Bring none and it stays plain.
What the mark becomes is not up to either of us.
I was his pupil. Halvard was the best carver who ever lived.
He cut one rune too deep, and we are all still inside it.
I remember people growing old. I don't miss it, and I would give it back tomorrow.
Seven deaths. Each time I check my hands afterwards, to see if they still know the marks.
Go well.

with.line: Light and Spark, ready-carved!

script.text: Light and Spark are ready-carved. Anything stronger, bring a blank to the runemaster.

then.text: Plain runes, carved by Hesper herself.
{item:rune-light}. It makes a light where you need one.
{item:rune-spark}. A small bolt. Enough to start with.
Right. What else?
The temple buys what the forges take.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:bone} you have.
I'll pay you 4 gold per {item:obsidian-shard} you have.
Right. What else?
Dagny, the temple clerk. I kept the harbour master's books before Wyrd.
One death in a hundred and thirty years. A bog imp. I'd rather not talk about it.
The temple closes at dusk.

with.line: Robes that hold a spell!

script.text: This one holds a spell better. That one is warmer. You can't have both.

then.text: Cloth for people who cast.
{item:cloth-tunic}. One point, and better than a shirt.
{item:tunic-of-flames}. It makes you a fire creature on the wheel.
{item:mantle-of-brambles}. It makes you nature on the wheel.
Right. What else?
Small things to wear with a robe.
{item:copper-ring}. One flat point, against anything.
{item:amulet-of-tides}. It makes you water on the wheel.
Right. What else?
Amaru. I came from the mountains across the sea and kept a sailcloth loom on the harbour.
The frost caves killed me eight times. The moss I dye with is worth it.
Halina makes coats that stop my customers' spells. I tell her she is weaving against me.
Come back when it's cold.

with.line: Potions! Bottles bought!

script.text: Jelly from a slime, ash from a wisp. Potions to buy, bottles and spoils to sell.

then.text: Drink one and you glow for an hour. Fourteen gold apiece. How many?

traded.text: Drink them somewhere dark. Anything else?

then.text: Two gold for every {item:empty-bottle}. How many have you got?
Slime jelly, and whatever a wisp leaves when it goes out. I brew with both.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:nature-slime-jelly} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:water-slime-jelly} you have.
I'll pay you 1 gold per {item:fire-slime-jelly} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:wisp-ash} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:wisp-dew} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:wisp-spore} you have.
As you like. What else?
Noor. I came from abroad as a spice merchant's buyer and ran his warehouse on the harbour. Pell the baker is my husband.
Nineteen deaths and most of them my own fault. A poison you've tasted is a poison you understand.
Write down what you learn, {partner}.

with.line: Bread off a Flame rune! Pies!

script.text: Baked on a Flame rune, not wood. Tastes cleaner. Don't tell the warriors.

then.text: Three gold a slice.
Two gold a loaf.
One gold per {item:apple}. I need them for the pies.
One gold per {item:berry}. Not if they're stale!
Pell. I baked ship's biscuit for the harbour. Noor at the apothecary is my wife.
Four deaths in a hundred and thirty years. I'm careful. I bake.
A troll killed me on the road once. It took a long time. I don't walk that road any more; Yeva carries my bread.
Come back when you're hungry!

with.line: Apples, a gold each!

script.text: Apples are a gold. Rabbit feet buy you one free.

then.text: One gold each.
One gold a handful.
One {item:rabbit-foot} for one {item:apple}. I bury them in the plots for luck.

traded.text: That's luck for a row. Anything else?

then.text: Suvi. I came from the cold north as a fisherman's wife. He drowned long before Wyrd.
I haven't eaten a fish in a hundred years. Good.
The wolves come out of the woods at night. Five times now. They take the throat first, if you want to know.
Mind the rows.

script.text: Evening. The lamps don't light themselves. Well, they nearly do.

then.text: I light every lamp in town at dusk with a flick of a Spark rune, and put them out at dawn.
Tobiah over in the warriors' town uses a taper. I taught him that. I've learned better since.
Casimir. I came here as a ship's boy and lit the harbour lamps for fifty years.
I lit the quay the night Wyrd took hold. I watched the lighthouse turn from yellow to white.
The light on the lighthouse is the only lamp on this island I'd put out if I could.
Stay where it's lit.

with.line: A gold for every rat tail!

script.text: You've died? What was it like? Everyone says it's bad but nobody says how.

then.text: Two gold a loaf, from my own flour.
I pay a bounty on rats. One gold a tail.
Mina. The miller's wife. My husband went across the sea to buy millstones a month before Wyrd.
Is there a man there who sells millstones? Is he old?
A hundred and thirty years and not once. I keep thinking it is going to be today.
Soot does the rats. Soot is the black one.
Be careful out there.

script.text: Tell me how it happened. Slowly. I'll read it back to you.

then.text: You have an entry already. Come and read it after the next time.

else.text: There. Your name, the day, and what you tell me you've lost.
Next time you wake, come and read it.

then.text: Anyone may tell me how they died and what they lost. I write it down, so after the next death they can read what they no longer remember.
It is forty volumes now.
Rosalind. I was a copyist in the harbour's counting houses. Anselm the pilgrim is my brother.
Twenty-eight deaths. I have read about every one of them, and remember almost none.
I have the entries of everyone who has climbed to Maren. They're short.
Come back and read it.

with.line: Mind the scaffolding!

script.text: I grow the timber, and then I build with it.

then.text: Orrin. Mason, born here. With my father I built the lower floors of Halvard's lighthouse.
I didn't know what it would be for. Nobody did.
Maren used to bring us bread and sit on the stones while we ate. She laughed a lot. I'd rather remember her like that.
People died of age here, once. My father did, the year before. I've died sixteen times. A roof had half of them.
Mind the scaffolding.

with.line: Have I told you about Maren?

script.text: Have I told you about Maren? I've told someone. Probably you.

then.text: You can't climb it alone. The upper floors need four of you, and four who trust each other.
She doesn't speak. She looks at you as if she is trying to remember your name. I know how that is.
I gave you something? I'm sure I did. Good.

else.text: I've an old sword I don't need. I don't remember why I have it.

traded.text: Take it. I won't remember giving it to you.

then.text: Fen. A deckhand, Tove says. I rowed in her whaleboat.
Three hundred and some deaths. I lost count, and then I lost the count.
Have I told you about Maren?

onEnter.text: Hey {traveller}, don't stray too far south. The woods bite.

script.text: Temple's open, {partner}. Forges are inside, the runemaster's at the back.

then.text: Taavi, day warden. I was in the harbour watch under Absalom. I chose the runes; he chose the drill yard.
Twenty-seven deaths. Two of those were Absalom. He was right to; it was a bad year.
Inside the town, yes. Wolves come out of the deep woods, and bog imps from the west. I go after both.
Keep to the road.

with.line: Stay under the lamps.

script.text: Late to be walking. Stay under the lamps.

then.text: Nadia, night warden. I came from abroad as a sailor and worked the harbour's night boats.
I carry my own light. Casimir says it makes his lamps look bad.
The wolves come to the plots after midnight. Eighteen deaths, and they were half of them.
Stay lit.

with.line: Want the tower? Nobody climbs it alone. Talk to me.

script.text: You want the tower? Good. You can't climb it alone. Nobody can.

then.text: You're on my list already. I'll find you three more.

else.text: Done. Give me time, and I'll find you three more.

then.text: I do. Absalom brought us here. I built the walls. We each did the part we were good at.
I ran the harbour's ropewalk before Wyrd. Forty people. This is easier.
Eleven times on the tower. Every one of them because somebody behind me ran.
Iolanthe thinks we should wait and see what breaking it does. I've waited a hundred and thirty years. I've seen.
Train. Then come back.

with.line: Up at dawn! Train it!

script.text: Up at dawn. A body is the one thing on this island no rune made. Train it.

then.text: Absalom. I was captain of the harbour watch. I led the people who refused runes east. Ragna runs the town; I run the drill.
Forty-four deaths. I learn something every time. Mostly what not to do.
Break the rune at the top of the tower and we all go back to dying once. That seems right to me.
The druids are not wicked. They are using the same knife that cut us.
Dawn. Drill yard.

with.line: Swords! Axes! Don't touch the hot ones.

script.text: Swords there. Axes there. Don't touch the hot ones.

then.text: Blades. Twenty for the plain one, fifty for a knight's, ninety-five for the tempered.
{item:iron-sword}. Straight, quick, asks Sharp 6 of you.

traded.text: Keep the edge off the stone. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: {item:knights-sword}. Truer than the iron and slower with it — Sharp 20.

traded.text: That one has a name where it came from. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Folded and quenched twice. Sharp 34, and worth every point of it.

traded.text: Best blade on the rack, and you know it. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Suit yourself. What else?
Axes, then. They land wilder than a blade and they land harder.
A woodsman's axe. Sharp 8, and it swings like a chore.

traded.text: Mind your shins. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: {item:broad-axe} — a hand's width of edge. Sharp 20 and Toughness 8 to hold it up.

traded.text: Heavy at the head, that's the point of it. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Two bits, two hands. Sharp 34 and Toughness 16, and nothing stands after it.

traded.text: You'll need both hands and both feet. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Fair enough. What else?
Blunt work. Nothing clever about it, and it never turns on the bone.
My own pattern. Blunt 5, and it does the same thing every time.

traded.text: It'll not surprise you. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Flanged head, iron through. Blunt 18.

traded.text: That'll dent a helm. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Both hands. Blunt 32 and Toughness 16 — it's more weight than weapon.

traded.text: Swing it once and mean it. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Right you are. What else?
Shields. A shield is held, so it costs you a hand and pays you back on every blow.
A {item:buckler}. One point of defence and it weighs nothing.

traded.text: Small, but it's there. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Boards and a rim. Two points, off every blow that lands.

traded.text: It'll split before you do. Anything else on the rack?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Three points. Carry one in each hand if you like — they add.

traded.text: Now let them come. Anything else?

cancel.text: It'll keep. Anything else on the rack?

then.text: Please yourself. What else?
A gold for every {item:bone}. It goes in the quench. How many?
Brannoc. I forged harpoons and anchor chain for the harbour. Tove the hunter is my sister.
Iron doesn't care what you believe. That's why I like it.
Come back when you've something to spend, {partner}.

with.line: Bows! If you can see it, you can hit it.

script.text: If you can see it you can hit it. Most of the time.

then.text: Reach is what you're paying for.
Two cells out to six, and a prayer. Ranged 5.
Two out to eight. Ranged 18.
Two out to ten, and a heavier arrow at the end of them. Ranged 32.
As you like. What else?
Selin. I came from a horse country across the sea as a merchant's guard, and stayed.
A cyclops, three times in a week. The third time I nearly had it.
Mateo says start with a spear. Mateo is wrong.
Aim low. They duck.

with.line: Old weapons bought! Something for anything!

script.text: Old sword? I'll give you something for it. Not much. Something.

then.text: What are you getting rid of?
I'll pay you 8 gold per {item:iron-sword} you have.
I'll pay you 8 gold per {item:simple-axe} you have.
I'll pay you 8 gold per {item:simple-hammer} you have.
I'll pay you 8 gold per {item:simple-bow} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:knights-sword} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:broad-axe} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:iron-mace} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:hunting-bow} you have.
Right. What else?
Mateo. I came from abroad as a sailor and joined the harbour watch.
I used to dream in another language. Lost it about my twentieth death.
A spear keeps them a step away. Out here a step is everything. I'm out of spears today, mind.
Keep your edge.

with.line: Armour that makes a spell miss!

script.text: This coat takes a fire spell and gives back half of it as heat. You'll be warm and alive.

then.text: Body first — it is the piece that is hit. Every point comes off every blow that lands.
{item:warded-robe}. One point, and six against anything arcane.

traded.text: Let them throw fire at you. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:padded-gambeson}. Two points, and four more against blunt.

traded.text: A club will not find much in that. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:leather-jerkin}. Two points, and two each against sharp blows and arrows.

traded.text: Turns a point better than it turns a hammer. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:chain-mail}. Three points, and four more against sharp blows.

traded.text: Rings turn an edge. They do nothing for a maul. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:steel-plate}. Five points, three each against sharp blows and arrows. The best I have.

traded.text: Now let them try. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: Right. What else?
Charms. None of them is armour and every one of them is defence — read the numbers.
{item:bone-charm}. Four against a fist or a jaw, and nothing else.

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: {item:jade-amulet}. Five against the arcane.

traded.text: Against a spell, nothing better this side of the robe. What else?

cancel.text: On the rail it stays. Anything else?

then.text: Suit yourself. What else?
Halina. I came from abroad and ran a sailmaker's loft. I learned what stops a spell by having spells cast at me.
Six times the druids burned me to test a lining. I paid them for it.
Come back before something bites you, {partner}, not after.

with.line: Smoked meat! Eat before the waste!

script.text: Raw meat in, smoked meat out.

then.text: Three gold a slab. Smoked all day.
Two gold.
One gold a cut.
Bertha. I came from abroad as a ship's provisioner. I fed the ships, and now I feed a town.
Eat before you go into the waste. A full belly mends you on the way.
A troll. It held me down and took its time. Ask anyone. Nothing worse.
Eat something first.

with.line: Claws, tusks, furs! I buy the lot!

script.text: Bear claw, troll tusk, yeti fur. Whatever you killed, I'll buy a piece.

then.text: Let's see it.
I'll pay you 2 gold per {item:snake-fang} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:imp-horn} you have.
I'll pay you 5 gold per {item:bear-claw} you have.
I'll pay you 6 gold per {item:troll-tusk} you have.
I'll pay you 8 gold per {item:skull-troll} you have.
I'll pay you 20 gold per {item:yeti-fur} you have.
I'll pay you 25 gold per {item:cyclops-eye} you have.
Right. What else?
Animal skulls, yes. That's a person's skull? Take it back to where they woke up and give it to them.
Magda. I kept a saddlery with Idris, and dug up the dead on the side. Then the dead stopped staying put.
Seven deaths. Twice to bears I was skinning that were not as dead as I thought.
Bring me something big.

script.text: Every lamp in this town lit with a real flame.

then.text: I light the lamps at dusk with a taper from the smithy, and put them out at dawn. Casimir uses a rune. Cheat.
Tobiah. I was Casimir's apprentice on the quay, and a junior in the watch.
A hundred and thirty years and I still look nineteen. Nobody takes me seriously.
Fell off a lamp post twice. Woke up at the bottom of it both times.
Mind the lamp posts.

with.line: Rope, flint, torches!

script.text: Rope, flint, oil, torches. Everything you need and nothing you don't.

then.text: Counted and on the shelf.
A {item:hand-lantern}. You can't go about in the dark without one.
A {item:sack}.
Right. What else?
Rukmini. I kept a ship's chandlery on the harbour. I came here because I trust what I can count.
Two deaths, both wolves, both on the road. I don't walk it now.
That's Ghee. He caught nine rats last week. He gets a share of the bounty.
Count your change.

onEnter.text: Hey {traveller}, don't stray too far north. Not yet.

then.text: No runes past this gate, {partner}. And don't go far into the waste yet.

else.text: No runes past this gate, {partner}. Not in your pack, not in your pocket.

then.text: I was born on this island. I watched it stop. One man and one rune did that.
Edda. I kept Halvard's door and the lighthouse stores. Absalom is my brother.
Hesper and I were friends. She still carves. So, no.
Fifty-three. You stop counting what it takes. You start counting what's left.
Keep the wall in sight.

script.text: Barrels, buckets and charcoal. Nothing that bursts.

then.text: Aurelio. A ship's carpenter who settled, and then the temple's best carver after Hesper.
A rune I shaped burst in my hand and burned a woman at the forge. She woke. I left that week.
I can still tell you how a mark is cut. I can't do it any more. I'm glad.
The druids aren't wrong. I just found out I couldn't be trusted with it.
Barrels don't burst.

with.line: Keep your feet under you!

script.text: Keep your feet under you. It's the only thing out there you can trust.

then.text: Nine trolls. Every one of them took longer than you'd think.
Bear caves, deep in the Greenwood. Don't go in alone, and don't go in hungry.
Sigrun. I was a lookout on the harbour wall. Then I hunted trolls, until the ninth.
They say you get used to dying. You don't. You just get used to being afraid.
Feet under you.

with.line: Waste is quiet today. That means nothing.

script.text: Waste is quiet today. That means nothing.

then.text: The Red Waste. Small things burn at the edge; worse things further in; the gorge is worst.
Now and then a troll comes up out of the gorge. Six of my deaths were trolls.
Gideon. I came from abroad as a stevedore and worked Ragna's ropewalk.
Forty-one deaths. You never stop hearing the troll ones.
Selin shoots past my ear. She hasn't hit me yet. Twice.
Keep the gate behind you.

script.text: Who's that? Oh. Go on, then.

then.text: Liv, night watch. I was an apprentice in Halina's sail loft. I came east because she did.
Fifteen. Three of them were the walls. Watch your step up here.
From up here you can see the light on the lighthouse all night. I don't look at it much.
Mind the dark.

with.line: Ale's three gold! Fight outside!

script.text: Come in out of it, {partner}. Ale's three gold a mug. Fight outside.

then.text: How many mugs?
Bertha's smoked meat. Three gold.
Pell's bread. Two gold.
Margit. I fished from Peregrine's boat and kept his accounts. I built this place so both towns could drink in one room.
A hundred and thirty years, and I've buried nobody. I've just watched them all come back through that door.
Druids at that end, warriors at this end. Everybody drinks the same ale.
Mind how you go, {partner}.

with.line: Best ale on the island!

script.text: Best ale on the island. Only ale on the island, but still.

then.text: Three gold a mug.
One gold a handful. They go in the brew.
One gold a cut, for the stew.
Kofi. Cabin hand, then a cook in Ifeoma's kitchen. I brewed the first ale after the harbour's breweries flooded.
Eleven deaths. A wolf at the door, last. At the door!
Don't let the druids heat your ale.

script.text: Buy me an ale and I'll tell you how I got past the first floor. *hic*

then.text: Fen and I went up together. Four of you, or don't go. *hic*
Maren looked at me. That was the worst of it. Not the dying.
A hundred and sixty. I used to mark every map with a little cross where it happened.
Rodrigo. I fished for Peregrine. Nobody needed fish after the harbour went, so I went into the caves. *hic*
Shame. *hic*

with.line: No runes in this house.

script.text: No runes in this house. Wipe your feet.

then.text: Bog root and honey. It mends you. Ten gold.
What did the bog give you?
I'll pay you 2 gold per {item:blue-mushroom} you have.
I'll pay you 3 gold per {item:imp-horn} you have.
Right. What else?
I sat with Maren while she went. She went well. Then he brought her back.
Thirty times the bog has had me. It gives me back every time, a bit less.
On a still night you can hear her from here, up in the tower. She sings. She doesn't know the words.
Mind the boards. Some are rotten.

with.line: Which ship was yours? I'll pray for her.

script.text: Which ship was yours, {partner}? I'll pray for her.

then.text: I've blessed you already. It doesn't wear off.

else.text: Bread for the road, and a blessing with it.

then.text: Anselm. I was lay brother of the harbour chapel. The chapel flooded, so the whole island is my chapel now.
Sixty times on these roads. I keep walking them.
I married Halvard and Maren, in the old chapel. Somebody should pray for her. She's had nobody but him.
Walk safely.

onEnter.text: Bread! Cheese! Lanterns! Wolves hunt at night, so buy a lantern!
Idris at the camp trades leather for skins!
Bog imps sleep round their fires at night. Go round!
Ale and a bed at Margit's inn, halfway down the road!

script.text: Bread from the druids, cheese from the warriors. Same price either way.

then.text: Two gold.
Two gold.
Three gold.
Hamid. I kept a stall on the quay. On the road I belong to neither town, and I sell to both.
Twenty-five deaths, all on this road. There's a bend after the lake. Walk wide.
Walk wide at the bend.

with.line: Letters! Parcels!

script.text: Letter for the druids? Give it here, I'm going that way.

then.text: Yeva. I came on a mail packet and ran messages for the harbour master. I still run.
A troll caught me on the road once. I've run faster ever since.
Pell's bread to the inn, Rukmini's letters to Mina, and whatever you pay me to carry.
A hundred and thirty years and my legs still think they're twenty-two. That part I don't mind.
Got to run.

name: Flame
description: Bone, carved with a rising flame. Kindles a fire where you point it.

name: Ember
description: Red crystal, carved with a diamond. Hurls a burning ember.

name: Frost
description: Blue crystal, carved with a cross of frost. Chills whatever it strikes.

name: Thorns
description: Green crystal, carved with a rising thorn. Strikes with a poisoned thorn.

name: Pyre
description: Red crystal, carved with a flame over logs. Bursts into fire around its target.

name: Rime
description: Blue crystal, carved with a saltire. Frosts everything around its target.

name: Bramble
description: Green crystal, carved with a tangle of stems. Grows poison briars around its target.

name: Verdance
description: Green crystal, carved with a sprouting shoot. Mends your wounds.

name: Bloom
description: Green crystal, carved with an opening bud. Heals you and draws out burns, chills and poison.

name: Cinder
description: Bone, carved with falling sparks. Flicks a cinder at a foe.

name: Sleet
description: Bone, scored with slanting rain. Flings a shard of sleet.

name: Barbs
description: Bone, carved with a barbed stem. Looses a hooked barb.

name: Light
description: Bone, carved with a beam. Makes your skin shine in the dark.

name: Spark
description: Bone, carved with a small cross. Snaps a spark of raw arcana at a foe.

name: Bolt
description: Lavender crystal, carved with a zigzag. Hurls a bolt of raw arcana.

name: Lance
description: Lavender crystal, carved with a spear. Drives a lance of raw arcana into a foe.

name: Inferno
description: Obsidian, carved with a blazing star. Sets everything around you alight.

name: Shatter
description: Obsidian, cut with a jagged crack. Bursts into ice around you.

name: Overgrowth
description: Obsidian, carved with a branching trident. Bursts into poison growth around you.

name: Stomp
description: Obsidian, carved with a blow on the ground. Shakes the earth and dazes everyone around you.

name: Berserk
description: Obsidian, carved with bared teeth. Fills you with a careless fury.

name: Crystallise
description: Obsidian, carved with a cold diamond. Cases you in ice.

name: Blossom
description: Obsidian, carved with two linked buds. You flower and mend fast.

particles.offsetX: 0.7 * (1 - 0.5 * LIFE) * cos(9 * AGE_SEC + PI * floor(2 * SEED))
particles.offsetY: 0.7 * (1 - 0.5 * LIFE) * sin(9 * AGE_SEC + PI * floor(2 * SEED))

name: Blank Arcane Stone
description: An uncut stone. The stone forge can shape it into a rune.

name: Climbing ivy (tall, wall to the north)
Climbing ivy (tall, wall to the west)
Bone Blank
description: Bone shaped for carving. Only the runemaster can cut a mark into it.

name: Crystal Blank
description: Crystal shaped for carving. It stays clear until an essence colours it.

name: Obsidian Blank
description: Obsidian shaped for carving. No material holds a stronger rune.

name: Fire Essence
description: A spark of fire, gathered from a creature of flame.

name: Water Essence
description: A spark of water, gathered from a creature of the tide.

name: Nature Essence
description: A spark of nature, gathered from a creature of the wild.

name: Rat Tail
description: Bald and pink, off a rat. The tanner buys them.

name: Bat Wing
description: Skin stretched over fingers, off a bat. The tanner buys them.

name: Rabbit's Foot
description: Soft, and lucky for somebody other than the rabbit. The tanner buys them.

name: Snake Fang
description: Hollow, with venom still in it. The tanner buys them.

name: Imp Horn
description: A twisted horn, off a bog imp. The tanner buys them.

name: Bear Claw
description: As long as a finger, and sharper. The tanner buys them.

name: Troll Tusk
description: Yellowed ivory, off a cave troll. The tanner buys them.

name: Yeti Fur
description: A white tuft that never gets wet. The tanner buys them.

name: Cyclops Eye
description: Still looking at you. The tanner buys them.

name: Slime Jelly
description: Green, and it wobbles. The potion seller buys it.

name: Water Slime Jelly
description: Blue, and cold to hold. The potion seller buys it.

name: Fire Slime Jelly
description: Red, and warm to hold. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Ash
description: What is left of an ember wisp. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Dew
description: What is left of a tide wisp. The potion seller buys it.

name: Wisp Spore
description: What is left of a moss wisp. The potion seller buys it.
